# Payment Terms, Purchase Receipts, and Asking Questions Three things were still open after [Part 4](/posts/bcsupplychain4/). The AI could not set payment terms. It could not receive goods. And it could not answer a question that needs many documents at once, such as "which vendor do we owe the most?". This post takes them in turn. The first was my mistake, the second is a genuine limit, and the third is a preview feature that I would approach carefully. ## 1. Payment terms: a gap in my configuration In an early run the AI could not set payment terms on a purchase order, and I wrote that Business Central offers no page for them, only unnamed codes. That was wrong. The page exists. I had not added it to the configuration. Adding it, read-only, took one line. Then I ran the request again, on a fresh copy of the practice company: ```PROMPT New order to Fabrikam, Inc. for MEXICO Swivel Chair, black on special terms. ``` The AI asked three things in one round. First, whether this meant a purchase order, because Fabrikam is a vendor and not a customer. Second, how many. Third, what "special terms" meant: a price, a payment term, both, or a discount. This time it could offer the real payment-term codes, because it could now read them. ![](assets/images/bcsupplychain5/terms-03-asks-special-terms.webp) *Question 3: payment terms, a special unit cost, both, or a line discount? It notes that it can set payment terms itself, with no step for the person* I answered: 34 chairs, 157.71 each, payment terms 1M(8D). The AI created the order, read it back, and reported what it had done and what it had not: ![](assets/images/bcsupplychain5/r4-payment-terms-agent-summary.webp) *Draft purchase order 106038: 34 × 157.71 = 5,362.14 plus 160.86 tax, payment terms 1M(8D), nothing received, stock unchanged at 502* It also flagged something I had not asked about: 157.71 is **6.49% above** the item's standard cost of 148.10, and Business Central accepts a cost above standard without comment, so someone should sign it off. I checked the order in the web client: ![](assets/images/bcsupplychain5/r4-payment-terms-in-bc.webp) *Purchase order 106038 for Fabrikam, Inc.: total 5,523.00, and the collapsed Invoice Details section shows 1M(8D)* | Field | Value | |---|---| | Order | 106038, Fabrikam, Inc. | | Line | 34 × MEXICO Swivel Chair, black at 157.71 = 5,362.14 | | Total including tax | 5,523.00 | | Payment terms | 1M(8D) | | Posted | No | The AI also rewrote its own note. The wiki said payment terms could only be changed by a person after the order was made. It had just proved that wrong, so it fixed the page. :::bullet-points What this shows - A missing ability can be a **configuration gap**, not a limit of the product. Check the list of pages before you write "cannot". - The AI **corrects its own notes** when the evidence changes. ::: ## 2. Purchase receipts: a person has to do them ```PROMPT Receive 13 AMSTERDAM Lamp from Graphic Design Institute. ``` The AI looked for an open order for the lamp, found none, and asked two questions. First the cost: it offered 42.80 (the item's standard cost) and 54.90 (the selling price, which it labelled as the wrong kind of number). Then whether to receive only or receive and invoice. I took the standard cost and receive-only. It then said, plainly: > "I could not receive the goods. Nothing was received and nothing was posted." ![](assets/images/bcsupplychain5/r4-receipt-draft-po.webp) *It created draft order 106039 for 13 lamps at 42.80, 556.40 plus 16.69 tax, 573.09 in total, so that the receipt is one step for a person* ```mermaid flowchart TD W["The AI wants to receive 13 lamps"] --> T{"What action exists?"} T --> RI["Only 'Receive and Invoice'
there is no receive-only action"] RI --> N{"Business Central needs the
vendor's invoice number"} N --> API["The purchase order page has
no field to store it"] API --> X(["Refused. The order stays a draft"]) X --> P(["A person posts the receipt
in the web client"]) ``` The reason is how the connection is built. In this practice company Actions were off everywhere, so there is no way to receive. And in an earlier test, with posting switched on in a throwaway copy, the one purchase action available was **Receive and Invoice**. There is no receive-only action, and the purchase order page has no field for the vendor's invoice number, which Business Central insists on. The post was refused and the order stayed a draft. So the AI prepared the order and wrote the steps: ![](assets/images/bcsupplychain5/r4-receipt-handover-what-is-left.webp) *The hand-over. Post Receive on the order (not Receive and Invoice). No Release step is needed first, because Business Central releases a single open order when you post it. The vendor's invoice comes later and is matched to the receipt* It also noticed that the only earlier purchase of this lamp was 17 at 46.05, so 42.80 is 7.1% lower. It gave me that as a point to check before posting. **The practical rule is simple: a person posts purchase receipts in the web client.** The AI learned that once and applied it from then on. It also looked up how to release an order on Microsoft Learn, which is the wiki, then Learn, then the web, working the way I set it up. ## Fireside chat: the standard pages and the data tools *Tonight's talk: two ways to ask Business Central a question.* **The standard pages:** I am the dependable one. List the orders, then list the lines of one order. Create a draft. Fix a quantity. **The data tools:** And I answer questions across documents. "Which vendor has the most open orders?" needs lines from all of them. **The standard pages:** How many tries did it take you? **The data tools:** Six failed queries before the right one. Names too long, a bad filter, a field that did not exist. **The standard pages:** I fail less often. Then again, you are read-only and preview, and Microsoft says charging is planned. **The data tools:** …(truncated)
